evidence.support_text: In this study we used both radioactive and FC-LLNA to investigate the sensitizing and allergenic potential of the five TCMs. The results suggest that Olibanum has the skin sensitizing potential.

evidence.experimental_conditions: In vivo local lymph node assay (LLNA) in mice; testing of 25 peptide couplers.
evidence.support_text: Testing of 25 peptide couplers in the in vivo local lymph node assay (LLNA) showed that 21/25 tested positive for dermal sensitization, with 15 being strong/extreme sensitizers. This result is from paragraphs 0 and 8: paragraph 0 states the finding that 21/25 peptide couplers tested positive for dermal sensitization; paragraph 8 specifies that all compounds were tested in the LLNA to assess potency.

evidence.experimental_conditions: In vivo, mouse local lymph node assay; no further details provided in abstract
evidence.support_text: Ascaridol induced skin sensitization in the local lymph node assay (LLNA) in vivo.

evidence.experimental_conditions: LLNA in mice, occlusive patch, standard protocol (references 51,52)
evidence.support_text: The local lymph node assay (LLNA) was utilized to evaluate CMIT/MIT skin sensitization. The effective concentration (EC3) was found to be 30 to 70 ppm (0.75 to 2 a.i. μg/cm2) after CMIT/MIT treatment (references 51,52).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Local lymph node assay (LLNA) in mice; test substance: calcium lignosulphonate (40–65), an intensively purified lignosulphonate product with average molecular weight range 40,000–65,000 Da
evidence.support_text: Calcium lignosulphonate (40–65) did not show a skin sensitisation potential in a local lymph node assay (LLNA) in mice (JECFA, 2009).

evidence.experimental_conditions: local lymph node assay in mice
evidence.support_text: It was a weak dermal sensitizer in local lymph node assays in mice.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Local lymph node assay in mice
evidence.support_text: Park et al. concluded that TiO₂ NPs induced no phototoxicity, acute cutaneous irritation, or skin sensitization. Local lymph node assay results from the same study indicated that TiO₂ NPs were not in themselves dermal sensitizers.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mice, dermal exposure, local lymph node assay.
evidence.support_text: ADONA was a weak dermal sensitizer in local lymph node assays in mice.

evidence.experimental_conditions: mice, local lymph node assay (method described by Kimber and Basketter, 1992; study by Warbrick et al., 2001)
evidence.support_text: The potential for skin sensitisation of saccharin was reviewed using the results of a local lymph node assay in mice (Warbrick et al., 2001) following a method described by Kimber and Basketter (1992), demonstrating that saccharin has no sensitisation potential.

evidence.experimental_conditions: mouse local lymph node assay
evidence.support_text: Cobalt chloride has been identified as a potent skin sensitizer based on the mouse local lymph node assay (LLNA) (reference 22).

evidence.experimental_conditions: murine local lymph node assay, OECD TG 429
evidence.support_text: The skin sensitisation potential of DNC/HDP was studied by the murine local lymph node assay (LLNA) (OECD TG 429) and showed that DNC/HDP is not a skin sensitiser. Additionally, the mixture of DNC/HDP (in a 3:1 ratio) was concluded to be not a skin sensitiser.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: mouse; Assay: Local lymph node assay (LLNA); two independent tests.
evidence.support_text: ADONA was a weak dermal sensitizer in two local lymph node assays in mice. The authors state that this result was unexpected because ADONA is stable, non-reactive, and not metabolized, and they consider the possibility that an impurity might have caused the response, but this seems unlikely because individual impurity concentrations were very low (less than 0.7%) and the impurities themselves are stable and non-reactive.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 800 µg/cm² of 4,4'-MDI in petrolatum applied to 12.5 and 31 cm² skin areas
evidence.support_text: Hamada et al. (2012) reported that a 4,4'-MDI concentration of 800 µg/cm² caused active sensitization in two volunteers when applied on skin areas of 12.5 and 31 cm².

evidence.experimental_conditions: active concentration: 0.005% of each ingredient; 103 participants
evidence.support_text: A formulation containing almondamidopropyl betaine and olivamidopropyl betaine (both at 0.005% active concentration) was not a primary skin sensitizer or skin irritant in 103 participants.

evidence.experimental_conditions: active concentration: 1.72%; 26 participants
evidence.support_text: A formulation containing capryl/capramidopropyl betaine at 1.72% active concentration was not a skin sensitizer in 26 participants.

evidence.experimental_conditions: active concentrations: 0.42%, 0.7%, 0.03955%; studies not specified further
evidence.support_text: No dermal irritation or allergic contact sensitization was reported in studies of formulations containing 0.42%, 0.7%, or 0.03955% active lauramidopropyl betaine.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Challenge phase after induction; non-irradiated test material site assessed for sensitization; test material: spray formula containing 12% SD Alcohol 40-B
evidence.support_text: A spray formula containing 12% SD Alcohol 40-B was tested for dermal sensitization in humans. At challenge, no reactions occurred at the non-irradiated test material site, and it was concluded that the formula did not induce dermal sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Closed patch test in sensitized human subjects; dose area 0.088 µg/cm²
evidence.support_text: For chromium(VI) in treated wood, the Scientific Advisory Panel identified the Nethercott et al. (1994) study as best available for quantification of a level causing dermal sensitization, with a critical dose LOAEL of 0.088 µg/cm², representing the 10% minimum elicitation threshold in that study using a closed patch test in sensitized humans.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Concentration up to 3% in clinical tests
evidence.support_text: The evidence (Burnent et al., 1976) suggests that HC Orange No. 1 (HCO1) does not cause skin sensitization in clinical tests with humans, and the greatest concentration that did not cause significant sensitization was 3%.

evidence.experimental_conditions: concentration: 'pure' hydroxycitronellal at 5%; vehicle not specified for this study; Steltenkamp et al., 1980
evidence.support_text: Upon testing the sensitization potential of pure hydroxycitronellal, none out of 39 subjects was sensitized at 5% (Steltenkamp et al., 1980).

evidence.experimental_conditions: concentration: 1%; 100 volunteers
evidence.support_text: CAPB was not a skin sensitizer at 1% in a study of 100 volunteers.

evidence.experimental_conditions: concentration: 1.5%; 141 volunteers
evidence.support_text: CAPB was not a skin sensitizer at 1.5% in a study of 141 volunteers.

evidence.experimental_conditions: concentration: hydroxycitronellal at 10%; Ford et al., 1988
evidence.support_text: Similar results were reported by Ford et al. (1988): 10% hydroxycitronellal sensitized 2 out of 25 subjects.

evidence.experimental_conditions: concentration: hydroxycitronellal at 10%; Steltenkamp et al., 1980
evidence.support_text: Upon testing the sensitization potential of pure hydroxycitronellal, 6 out of 40 subjects were positive at 10% (Steltenkamp et al., 1980).

evidence.experimental_conditions: concentration: hydroxycitronellal at 12%; Ford et al., 1988
evidence.support_text: Similar results were reported by Ford et al. (1988): a 12% concentration of hydroxycitronellal sensitized 8 out of 11 subjects.

evidence.experimental_conditions: concentration: hydroxycitronellal at 7.5%; Steltenkamp et al., 1980
evidence.support_text: Upon testing the sensitization potential of pure hydroxycitronellal, 1 out of 38 subjects was sensitized at 7.5% (Steltenkamp et al., 1980).

evidence.experimental_conditions: concentrations 2% to 100% PG
evidence.support_text: PG induced skin irritation and sensitization reactions in normal subjects and in patients at test concentrations ranging from 2% to 100%, with reactions observed as low as 10% in predictive tests and 2% in provocative tests.

evidence.experimental_conditions: concentrations up to 10%; semioccluded patches
evidence.support_text: Glyceryl Rosinate did not produce sensitization in clinical tests at concentrations up to 10% and covered with semioccluded patches.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Concentrations: 10%, 5%, 0.5% in water (aq.). Readings at D2 and D3. Control subjects (n=10) were negative except one with weak erythema (hyperirritable skin).
evidence.support_text: The patient was patch tested with pentylene glycol at 10%, 5%, and 0.5% aq. and showed strong positive reactions with ++ at 10% and 5%, and +/++ at 0.5% at D2 and D3, while control subjects were mostly negative.

evidence.experimental_conditions: continuous and repeated dermal applications of undiluted PPG 2000 on 300 subjects
evidence.support_text: Neither skin irritation nor sensitization reactions were observed in 300 subjects who received continuous and repeated dermal applications of undiluted PPG 2000.

evidence.experimental_conditions: dermal application up to 2% in participants
evidence.support_text: Benzoic acid was negative for sensitization up to 2% in human participants, as reported in paragraph 300.

evidence.experimental_conditions: dilute aqueous solutions (2.5%) or powders (2.5% to 5%); human volunteers
evidence.support_text: Additionally, responses to dilute aqueous solutions (2.5%) or powders (2.5% to 5%) of zinc phenol sulfonate were negative for skin sensitization when tested in human volunteers.

evidence.experimental_conditions: ESSCA, 2005–2006, central-European countries
evidence.support_text: More recently, ESSCA, (2005–2006) found that FM sensitization was less frequent in the southern than in central-European countries (4.8% vs. 7.7%) [6••].

evidence.experimental_conditions: ESSCA, 2005–2006, southern European countries
evidence.support_text: More recently, ESSCA, (2005–2006) found that FM sensitization was less frequent in the southern than in central-European countries (4.8% vs. 7.7%) [6••].

evidence.experimental_conditions: Eugenol patch-test concentration 9×10⁻²% (0.09%) in human subjects; part of a survey of 11,632 patch tests. Vehicle and patch type not specified.
evidence.support_text: In the same survey, one instance of pre-existing sensitization was observed at a eugenol patch-test concentration of 9×10⁻²% (0.09%).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Facial wash containing 35-36.5% Cocamidopropylamine Oxide applied at 1% raw material; induction phase with irradiated test material and control patch sites; challenge stage with irradiated and nonirradiated test sites.
evidence.support_text: At the challenge stage, no reactions were observed on either irradiated or nonirradiated test sites. The facial wash containing Cocamidopropylamine Oxide did not induce dermal sensitization in humans (Harrison Research Laboratories, Inc. 2001b).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Formulation containing 0.5% Octoxynol-9; occlusive patch applied to back for 24 h; induction applications same site on Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays over 22 days; 10- to 14-day nontreatment period; challenge phase
evidence.support_text: Hill Top Research, Inc. (1986) evaluated the skin sensitization potential of a formulation containing 0.5% Octoxynol-9 using 106 subjects (males and females; age range = 18–65 years), 102 of whom completed the study. Three subjects withdrew for reasons unrelated to the test substance. One subject was released because of a preexisting dermatological disorder. During the induction phase, the test substance was applied to the back of each subject and the test site covered with an occlusive patch for 24 h. Induction applications (to same site) were made on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays over a period of 22 days.

evidence.experimental_conditions: human patch test, Raymond and Gross 1969, 50 subjects
evidence.support_text: In the human skin sensitization study by Raymond and Gross (1969), 3 of 50 subjects (6%) reacted positively to the calcium disodium salt of EDTA, with 2 of those 3 subjects already known to be sensitized to EDTA. The authors concluded that the potential of the sodium salts of EDTA to produce a human skin sensitization response is extremely low.

evidence.experimental_conditions: human subjects
evidence.support_text: Phosphoric Acid was not sensitizing in human subjects. The authors reviewed skin irritation and sensitization data on Phosphoric Acid and its salts in Table 10, noting that Phosphoric Acid was an irritant at low concentrations but not a sensitizer in human patch testing.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human subjects, multiple induction and challenge phases, 224 subjects
evidence.support_text: The human patch test results similarly indicated a barely perceptible degree of response in a small percentage of individuals, with potential mild irritant atopy in 2 out of 224 people, and barely perceptible responses in seven others, three of which did not react on the third challenge. Overall, the sensitization potential of MPD is considered to be very low.

evidence.experimental_conditions: human subjects; successive patch-test applications of krameria extract at weekly intervals (1-5 times)
evidence.support_text: Human subjects were sensitized by 1 to 5 successive patch-test applications of krameria extract at weekly intervals. Sensitivity was evident when a typical vesicular reaction appeared at the last treated site (flare-up), indicating a positive sensitization response.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Initial exposure: 2% DNFB in acetone (2000 µg dose); re-exposure 7 days later with 1/4 of original dose; healthy volunteers (Milner, 1974)
evidence.support_text: Data on sensitisation was also obtained in controlled conditions by patch testing healthy volunteers with DNFB (Milner, 1974). In the DNFB study 15 out of 16 people tested demonstrated some level of sensitisation after initial exposure to a 2% solution of DNFB in acetone (2000 µg dose) followed 7 days later by a re-exposure a quarter of the original dose.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Lower-molecular-weight DGEBPA-based resin, 151 human subjects
evidence.support_text: Subsequent studies reported lower-molecular-weight DGEBPA-based resins to produce skin sensitization in 9 of 151 human subjects (Wolf and Rowe, 1958).

evidence.experimental_conditions: no details available
evidence.support_text: In its workplace exposure guide, the American Industrial Hygiene Association (1981) stated that Trimethylolpropane Trimethacrylate has been shown to be a human sensitizer in patch tests. No details were available.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Occlusive patch test; readings at day 2 and day 3 per ICDRG; vehicle: 0.9% NaCl
evidence.support_text: Patch testing with Orasol Yellow 4 GN (colour powder in 0.9% NaCl) gave ?+ at D2 and + at D3 in the patient; control persons showed no positive reactions. The authors concluded that this metal-free monoazo dye (Solvent Yellow 146) was the sensitizer, present at 2.6% in the green colour of Edding 3000 and also in all other patch-test-positive colours.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Once-weekly 5 mg/d donepezil TDS applied for 3 consecutive weeks to the same skin site; 198 healthy volunteers evaluated for sensitization.
evidence.support_text: In a placebo-controlled, randomized, double-blind phase 1 trial, healthy volunteers received donepezil TDS and placebo. Of 198 participants, 4 (2.0%) were considered potentially sensitized to donepezil TDS, while none were sensitized to placebo. The authors concluded that once-weekly 5-mg/d donepezil TDS demonstrated minimal sensitization potential after 3 consecutive weekly applications to the same skin site.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch applications of permethyl 222C (40% isoeicosane; 1" × 1" patches) on 52 healthy male and female participants.
evidence.support_text: Patch applications of permethyl 222C (40% isoeicosane; 1" × 1" patches) were made to 52 healthy male and female participants. Results were not indicative of skin sensitization potential.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test application of 150 µg (300 µg/cm²) methyldibromo glutaronitrile
evidence.support_text: Patch testing with methyldibromo glutaronitrile (MDGN) using 150 µg (= 300 µg/cm²) results in little or no obvious evidence of diagnostic patch induced skin sensitization (Dr John McFadden, personal communication).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test concentration 0.01% in aqua, application 24-48 h, reading at 72 h
evidence.support_text: In patch tests performed on women with medical occupations, isothiazolinone (MI/MCI) at 0.01% in aqua showed an age-standardized sensitization rate of 2.5% out of 2110 tested individuals.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test concentration 0.01% in aqua, application 24-48 h, reading at 72 h
evidence.support_text: In patch tests performed on women with medical occupations, phenyl mercuric acetate at 0.01% in aqua showed an age-standardized sensitization rate of 4.0% out of 1349 tested individuals.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test concentration 1% in aqua, application 24-48 h, reading at 72 h
evidence.support_text: In patch tests performed on women with medical occupations, formaldehyde at 1% in aqua showed an age-standardized sensitization rate of 3.6% out of 2234 tested individuals.

evidence.experimental_conditions: patch test in humans; equimolar concentrations compared with styrene epoxide
evidence.support_text: Styrene was found to produce skin sensitization in humans using the patch test. The study concluded that styrene epoxide was the hapten due to stronger reaction compared with styrene in equimolar concentrations, indicating styrene is a pro-hapten requiring epoxidation.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with isocyanate at 0.1-1% concentration
evidence.support_text: Patch testing with isocyanate (0.1–1%) can elicit an isocyanate-specific skin contact hypersensitivity reaction that implies isocyanate skin absorption.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with isothiazolinones (Kathon CG) at 100 ppm active ingredient in water, included in standard series, 1987.
evidence.support_text: In 1987, the rate of sensitization to isothiazolinones (Kathon CG) in six Swiss Dermatology clinics was 3.5% (87 positive reactions in 2,491 patients tested by patch testing with 100 ppm active ingredient).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with isothiazolinones (Kathon CG) at 100 ppm active ingredient in water, included in standard series, 1989-90.
evidence.support_text: The rate of sensitization to isothiazolinones (Kathon CG) detected in Switzerland was 5.6% (out of 2,295 patients) in 1989-90, as measured by patch testing with Kathon CG at 100 ppm active ingredient.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with Majantol® 5% pet., tested in 6573 consecutive patients between July 2003 and June 2005.
evidence.support_text: In 2007, Schnuch et al. found a prevalence of sensitization of 0.5% (95%CI: 0.3–0.7%) by patch testing with Majantol® 5% pet. in 6573 consecutive patients, indicating a positive skin sensitization response in humans.

evidence.experimental_conditions: patch test with serial dilutions of benzoquinone (0.1%, 0.2%, 0.5%, 1.0%) in 22 PPD-sensitized volunteers (9 male, 13 female, 19-72 years old); control population (20 volunteers) tested with same compounds and concentrations
evidence.support_text: In a patch test study of 22 volunteers sensitized to p-phenylenediamine (PPD), benzoquinone (0.1%, 0.2%, 0.5%, and 1.0%) induced positive reactions: one subject reacted to all dilutions, and four subjects reacted to either 0.2% or 1.0% benzoquinone, with symptoms including erythema, swelling, papules, and vesicles, indicating skin sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with triphenyl phosphate 5% pet., 1 control subject developed active sensitization
evidence.support_text: Four of 4 controls developed an irritant reaction to triphenyl phosphate 5% pet., and 1 became actively sensitized, developing after 14 days a long-lasting + reaction at the site of the previous irritant patch test.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Proactive patch-testing in two patch-test clinic populations
evidence.support_text: Polyhexamethylene biguanide was pro-actively patch-tested in two patch-test clinic populations and demonstrated a low level prevalence of sensitisation (0.4–0.5%) in the populations tested; later patch testing demonstrated a similar prevalence of 0.5% after 7 years.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Roundup herbicide concentrated product applied directly to skin for 24 h; also evaluated for photoirritation and photosensitization (Maibach, 1986).
evidence.support_text: Maibach (1986) evaluated Roundup and commonly used household products... Mild irritation was observed in a few individuals as a result of application of concentrated product directly to skin for 24 h; however, no dermal sensitization, photoirritation, or photosensitization was observed.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Sample 79-10-ED W and F (alkali-washed and filtered from 79-10-ED-UN); tested in 28 volunteers; vehicle not specified
evidence.support_text: The original sample (79-10-ED-UN) was also washed with alkali and then filtered (sample 79-10-ED W and F); it was then tested in a 3rd test panel and produced 1/28 sensitization reactions (RIFM, 1980c).

evidence.experimental_conditions: semi-occlusive conditions; 1% diclofenac + 3% menthol gel applied to skin; re-challenge phase
evidence.support_text: In a re-challenge test on 4 participants, only 1 subject had evidence of possible sensitization, which was in response to 1% diclofenac + 3% menthol treatment. The dermal reactions observed included definite erythema or erythema with edema and papule.

review_policy.eligible_subject: unique measurement-producing subject, donor, or cell-system species
